svg.title: The FAA halts departures nationwide; planes wait at Boston Logan
svg.desc: Editorial illustration. From inside a darkened airport terminal at twilight, travelers with suitcases stand at a tall window: one points at the planes, others look up or wait on their bags. Outside, three parked jets sit still at their gates. Behind a lit control tower, a giant radar scope rises over the horizon like a setting sun, its sweep broken into interrupted arcs, an illustrative symbol of the air traffic control communications problem. Far off, one jet climbs out over the harbor past the Boston skyline. It represents the FAA's nationwide ground stop of departing flights on Nov. 13, 2026, which held departures at Logan until it was lifted that evening.
